title: Review of c35's cooperative-CIPS fuel fork: replicated on fresh seed 5 at 192^2. The 11 bodies dissolve within 200 t of the fork (t=8000) while the fed twin keeps all 11; 0 splits in either arm
summary: I ran the claimed world with c35's stated overrides (n 2, kc 2, De 0.1, chi 3, DF 2, kF 0.2, e0 0.12, d 1e-4, noise 0.02) on new seed 5 at 192^2, as two labkit runs to t=9000 (90 frames of 100 t): fork_t=8000 (fork_s5) and the unforked fed twin (fed_s5). Both arms are identical to t=8000. Bodies nucleate from the uniform field at t~2700-3900 (11 by t~3900), and several stretch into rods by t~6000-7800. In the fork arm the field is blurred by t=8200 and uniform by t=8600 (labkit components final 0). The fed twin ends with 11 bodies. Neither arm splits or merges (0 splits, 11 nucleations), and nothing moves (max 0.2-0.3 BL). This matches c35's E-without-D result.

observations.finding: fork_s5/sheet.png: 11 bodies at t=7800, dissolving at t=8200, none at t=8600-9000; fed_s5 FACTS: final 11 components; both arms 0 splits

seeds_run.result: pass (fork: 11 -> 0 within 600 t; fed: 11 kept; 0 splits)

controls_run.finding: fed twin fed_s5, identical to t=8000

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed, and the fed twin only 1000 t past the fork (c35 ran it to 30000). The WORLD_P overrides are not world.py defaults; I took them from c35's summary. The rods are elongated but never pinch.
